# 1 Clement Chapter 20 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 20

**[TRANSLATOR'S NOTE: Chapter 20 is the magnificent cosmic-order hymn of 1 Clement. Clement surveys all creation — heavens, earth, sea, seasons, tides, living creatures — and finds in each one an example of ordered submission to the Creator's will. The theological argument is: creation obeys God; Corinthians should too. The passage shows clear influence from Stoic cosmology and is among the most beautiful prose passages in Ante-Nicene literature.]**

**20:1** The heavens, moving under his government, are subject to him in peace. Day and night run the course appointed by him, not hindering each other.

**20:2** The sun and the moon and the dancing stars revolve in harmony according to his appointment in their appointed courses, and in nothing transgress his ordinance.

**20:3** The earth, bearing fruit in fulfillment of his will at the proper seasons, puts forth the food that supplies men and beasts and all living things upon it without dissension and altering nothing of his decrees.

**20:4** The inscrutable depths of the abyss and the indescribable regions of the lower world are controlled by the same ordinances.

**20:5** The basin of the boundless sea, gathered together by his workmanship into its reservoirs, does not pass beyond its appointed bounds, but does as he appointed to it;

**20:6** For he said: "Thus far shall you come, and your waves shall be broken within you." [Job 38:11]

**20:7** The impassable ocean, and the worlds beyond it, are governed by the same decrees of the Master.

**20:8** The seasons of spring and summer and autumn and winter succeed each other in peace.

**20:9** The stations of the winds at the proper seasons perform their service without failure. The ever-flowing fountains, created for enjoyment and health, without fail give their breasts for the life of men.

**20:10** The smallest of the living creatures come together in peace and concord.

**20:11** All these things the great Creator and Sovereign Lord of all willed to exist in peace and concord, showing his bounty to all things, but most abundantly to us who have fled for refuge to his mercies through our Lord Jesus Christ,

**20:12** to whom be glory and majesty forever and ever. Amen.

---

*EMET: "dancing stars" (*chorous*) — the cosmic dance is a Greek philosophical image for the order of the heavenly bodies. "Inscrutable depths of the abyss" — Clement's knowledge of the sea's depths is striking. "Breasts" of fountains (v.9) is a vivid, embodied metaphor for springs. "Most abundantly to us" — the cosmic argument pivots to the particular mercy shown to Christians.*
